fails: The banner doesn't fully obey the 8-bit style: the glowing headline, soft moon halo, faint grid and gradients are smooth effects, not hard pixels. The text is vector monospace, not pixel font.
The props are small and scattered in the left and right margins. The chronometer, almanac, sextant and compass don't connect to the ship, so the composition reads as a row of icons around the ship.

The captions are tiny and low-contrast: 'CHRONOMETER K1', 'SEXTANT DE BORDA', 'COMPASS ROSE' and 'HMS RESOLUTION' are dark gold or blue on navy and illegible. The 'K1' label is clipped under the clock. 'COMPASS ROSE' and 'DE BORDA' collide with their icons.
The ship is a crude, boxy hull with uneven mismatched sails and a stray oar-like stick at the bow. It is low-contrast and sits on the horizon with a mostly empty sea beneath it.
The ghost '1776' watermark in the sky is nearly invisible and adds nothing. The compass rose looks like a lumpy cookie rather than a compass.
At thumbnail size the headline turns to a thin yellow smear. The subtitle is unreadable. Only the yellow frame, the moon and a vague ship shape survive. The small props and all captions are lost.
critic.next_change: Enlarge the ship to about twice its size and centre it, with a bigger, higher-contrast pixel-grid hull and cleaner sails. Remove the tiny captions and the ghost '1776', and make the headline a chunkier blocky pixel font with no glow so it survives at 120px.
critic.works: The scene is clearly nautical and astronomical. A pixel-art ship under a night sky with a full moon, stars, a constellation line and a comet. The subject props match the article: a K1 chronometer labelled Larcum Kendall, a Borda sextant, a compass rose, the Nautical Almanac, and HMS Resolution. The yellow glowing headline is bold and readable at full size, and the dark navy ground with gold accents gives a coherent value structure.

fails: Dickinson's right arm is clipped by the parchment edge, and a stray quill/cane shard floats at his hand. A second loose white stick-and-fragment cluster sits in the bottom-right corner, reading as a rendering artifact.
The '1776' numerals are dark brown on a dark green-black ground, so they have almost no contrast. They are also mis-spaced: the '6' is cramped and the digits don't read cleanly as a date.
The '9/13' counter and its 'VOTES TO PASS' label are tiny, and the label overlaps the green progress bar and is unreadable. The key doctrine (a 9-of-13 supermajority) is the weakest-reading element.

The parchment holds a wall of identical lines of fake text and takes up about a third of the canvas without carrying meaning. Its 'ARTICLES OF CONFEDERATION' heading is microscopic and sits over a dark bar that doesn't align with it.

The ring of stars is irregular, with uneven spacing and stray green specks, so it doesn't read as a deliberate 13-star circle. The bottom row of 13 colored books is flat and busy, and it competes with the focal point.

At 120px the headline and subtitle turn to illegible smudges. The figure survives only as a small blue blob next to a tan rectangle, and the stars and counter vanish into the dark ground. The thumbnail has no single dominant focal point.
critic.next_change: Cut the parchment to about half its width and enlarge Dickinson. Then replace the tiny '9/13' counter with a large, bright, high-contrast '9/13' (about 3x current size) centered in the star ring. Drop the unreadable 'VOTES TO PASS' label and the dark-brown '1776' so the figure and the vote count become the two clear focal points.
critic.works: The subject is clearly this article: a white-haired Dickinson in a navy coat labeled 'J. DICKINSON', an Articles of Confederation parchment, a '9/13 VOTES TO PASS' counter ringed by 13 gold stars, and 13 colored state-books along the bottom. The pixel-art style is honored (blocky figure, chunky text, CRT scanlines, vibrant state colors). The title bar is legible at full size and the vote-threshold concept is on topic.

fails: Palette is dark and muddy: a near-black purple background and a heavy vignette/scanline overlay. It reads as dim, not the 'vibrant colors' the style card asks for.

The title is the only large text, and it is low-contrast dark gold on near-black. The subtitle line 'FREDERICK NORTH, EARL OF GUILFORD...' is dark teal on black and almost unreadable even at full size; it also sits on or clipped by the bottom red rule.
Too much small HUD text for a banner: POLITICAL WILL, LOW, YEAR: 1776, STAGE: BOSTON EVACUATED, the BRITAIN vs COLONIES line, and the speech bubble. All of it turns to mush at thumbnail size.
The speech bubble is tiny, with text wrapped awkwardly ('WON...' on its own line). Its tail overlaps the figure's head and the golden pillar, and the bubble crowds the window row.

The focal point is weak. The North figure is small and low, with a stray stick-like arm or quill, and he competes with the lit building, the crown, the flags, the cannon and the red '1776'. The eye has nowhere to land.

The red '1776' in the upper left is dark red on dark purple, so it is low contrast. The Union Jack is distorted: its diagonals look broken and mismatched. The American flag has a canton of 13 star dots, but it is anachronistic for 1776 and is not shown beside the flag the Continental Army used.

At 120px the silhouette is lost: the building, figure and crown merge into a dark smear, and the title and everything else is illegible. The thumbnail is basically a dark rectangle with a few yellow window dots.
critic.next_change: Cut the HUD clutter (the meter, YEAR/STAGE text, the 'BRITAIN vs COLONIES' line and the subtitle) and brighten the scene: a saturated sky-blue or teal background in place of the near-black purple, with the vignette and scanlines removed. Scale up the North figure and the crown, and set the title in large, high-contrast, cream-on-dark pixel lettering so both the silhouette and the headline survive at 120px.
critic.works: The subject is clearly identified. It shows a powdered-wig figure in a red coat, Parliament with a clock tower, a Union Jack facing a US flag, a crown for George III, and a 'political will: LOW' meter. These match North's story: a reluctant PM, the Boston evacuation, and the Crown. The pixel-art chunky shapes and the 'stage' game-HUD framing fit the 8-bit style. The gold title bar is legible at full size.

fails: The right-hand ship is a set of grey blocks that overlap the building's glow and the redcoats' flag and muskets. It is an unreadable muddy cluster rather than a ship.
The footer text 'AMERICAN REVOLUTION' is clipped at the right edge of the canvas.
The bottom HUD band uses very low-contrast text (dark red 'BRITISH FORCE' and dark blue 'MILITIA DEFENSE' on dark green) that is nearly illegible and adds clutter.

The style card calls for crisp pixel graphics, but the headline and labels are smooth anti-aliased vector type with a glow, not pixel or bitmap lettering. The scanline and vignette overlay also softens the pixel edges.

The title wraps awkwardly: 'RAID' sits on its own line with a small orphaned '&', then 'BATTLE OF RIDGEFIELD' is set in a different colour and size. The three-tier hierarchy is fragmented and the top-left date chip crowds the title.
At 120px only the large yellow 'THE DANBURY RAID' headline and the glowing building read. The soldiers, trees, cannon and ship turn to mush, and the subtitle and footer are illegible.
The wagon and cannon in the middle foreground is an indistinct grey-and-brown blob. Trees and figures are evenly spaced and static, so the scene has little sense of battle.
critic.next_change: Replace the grey block-cluster ship and the low-contrast bottom HUD band with a clean, higher-contrast pixel silhouette of a ship (dark hull, two light sails) positioned clear of the building and flag, and pull 'AMERICAN REVOLUTION' fully inside the canvas.
critic.works: The burning building with an orange glow and pixel flames is the focal point and reads as the Danbury depot. The blue-coated militia face the red-coated British, and the ship masts on the right nod to the retreat to the ships. The layout is clear and the palette is vibrant, with a good dark-night value structure. The 8-bit look is mostly convincing.

fails: Style: the rendering is blocky vector rectangles, not true pixel art. The ship sails and hulls, the soldiers, and the text use smooth edges and anti-aliased glows. The palette is also dim and muddy (dark navy, olive, black) instead of vibrant.

Craft: the top-right HUD overlaps. 'FORTS: ♥♥♥' is drawn over three dark red squares and is partly illegible. The smoke plume over Fort Montgomery sits on top of its flag, so the flag is garbled. A grey smoke blob sits on the lead ship's hull and a stray gray pixel floats under the soldiers.

Craft: composition is scattered. The forts, soldiers, and ships are small, evenly weighted, and spread across a big empty purple sky, so there is no strong focal point. The soldiers float above the water with no boat or ground under them. The ships are cropped awkwardly against the right hills, and the dark bottom third is dead space.

Craft: the bottom text stack is crowded. The title, subtitle, and tagline are three separate lines. The date appears twice (the OCT 6, 1777 box and the tagline). The tiny '~ HUDSON RIVER CHAIN ~' label and the fort name labels are too small to read.

Thumbnail: at 120px the scene collapses into a dark mass. The forts and ships are tiny dim blobs. The title is the only element that partly reads, and the subtitle and tagline are mush. Overall contrast is low, with a black frame eating the edges.
critic.next_change: Redraw the scene larger and brighter on a strict pixel grid. Scale the forts and the lead ship up to about 2x, fill the empty sky with a bright gradient or a sunset band, and drop the HUD clutter, the duplicate date line, and the tiny labels. Remove the smoke over the flag and put the soldiers on a boat or the shoreline. That gives a single big silhouette that survives at 120px.
critic.works: The subject is specific and readable: two gold forts on the left (one burning), a row of redcoats in the middle, British ships on the right, and a river chain across the water. The arcade-HUD framing (PLAYER/ENEMY, FORTS: hearts) and the glowing yellow/orange title fit the 8-bit game-screen concept. The stepped green hills and blocky flags are convincingly pixel-art. The title is correctly spelled and not clipped at full size.

fails: The title block is broken. The 'MADRID · OCT 30, 1778' line is clipped by the panel's top edge and collides with the 'RAQUEL' headline, so its top half is cut off.
'RAQUEL' is small and low-contrast (grey on dark navy) for a headline. It takes up only a small part of the banner.
The yellow comedy mask is cut off by the right frame edge, and the red tragedy mask almost touches it. The pair looks accidental rather than composed.

The '★ TRAGEDIA · 5 ACTS · 1778 ★' line sits on top of the king's legs and overlaps the figure. The 'by GARCÍA DE LA HUERTA' text is near-invisible dark-on-dark, and the empty box behind it looks like a leftover.

The castle is one large flat navy mass with almost no value separation from the sky, so it reads as a dead area covering half the banner. The moon is a soft blurred glow, not crisp pixels, and the gradients and glow break the clean-pixel style rule.
The figures are rendered with smooth edges and drop shadows. The yellow diamond floating above the castle is unexplained.

At 120px the headline and every other line of text turn to mush and cannot be read. Only the castle block, the moon and the red-and-purple figures survive, as small blobs. The subject is hard to identify at that size.
critic.next_change: Rebuild the bottom-left title panel. Make it taller, move the 'MADRID · OCT 30, 1778' line fully inside it with clear padding above 'RAQUEL', and set 'RAQUEL' much larger in bright white or yellow with a dark pixel outline. Then delete the tiny HUD lines (the 'TRAGEDIA' line and the empty 'by GARCÍA DE LA HUERTA' box) so nothing overlaps the figures.
critic.works: The subject is specific and recognisable. A crowned, bearded king in a red tabard with a gold cross stands beside a woman in purple, in front of a night-time castle, which fits Alfonso VIII and Raquel in Toledo. The tragedy and comedy masks point to the theatre premiere. The palette is saturated and retro (navy, gold, red, purple), and the HUD-style 'TRAGEDIA · 5 ACTS · 1778' and 'PRESS START' text suit the 8-bit game look. The two figures are the clear focal point, and the glowing moon adds some value contrast.

fails: The HOLLYWOOD lettering sits in the upper-left, unanchored to any hillside. The M is malformed and collides with the Y. It competes with the real title for attention and reads as an error.
The 'DIES AT 83' subtitle is jammed against the magenta rule below it, with almost no padding, so it looks clipped.

The scene is scattered. The blue BH 90210 plate floats in empty space, the crown-on-pedestal object is ambiguous, and the two side shelves of colored blocks have no clear meaning. There is no single focal point, because the TV, the Hollywood lettering and the crown all compete.

The glowing blur on the type, scanline texture and soft gradients break the 'clean pixel graphics' rule. The mountains are smooth vector polygons, not pixel-stepped shapes. The pink figure is tiny and crude.

At 120px the TV and the Hollywood lettering survive as blobs, but the headline and subtitle turn to mush. The footer strips are unreadable, and the pink figure and crown vanish. The banner is dark and low-contrast overall.
The bottom credit strip is dim olive on black, with very low contrast even at full size.
critic.next_change: Remove or fix the floating HOLLYWOOD lettering, either by deleting it or by redrawing it as a clean block-pixel sign with a correct M on the hillside. Then enlarge the headline and give it a pixel-stepped outline with no glow, with clear padding above the 'DIES AT 83' line, so the title reads at thumbnail size.
critic.works: The subject is clear: a TV set with a pink silhouette, a Hollywood sign, a BH 90210 plate, and a crown on a pedestal for the 'king of TV' idea. The palette is vivid neon (yellow, magenta, cyan) on a dark purple ground, which suits the retro 8-bit brief. The header and footer text are legible at full size and the show titles anchor it to Spelling's career.

fails: The '957,000 COPIES #1 BILLBOARD' line collides with its yellow outlined box. The box is narrower than the text, so the '9' and the 'D' poke out past its edges, and the '9' is partly clipped by the box border and the left column. This is a visible craft error.
The bear's graduation cap is missing or hidden. The rainbow sits directly on its head, with a stray yellow tassel fragment floating above, so the graduation motif is weak and the tassel looks broken.

The bear's anatomy is awkward: the neck and torso are a blocky orange mass, the hands are cropped and clipped at the arms, and the diploma is an ambiguous cream rectangle with a red 'T'. The pixel grid also looks inconsistent, with soft glow and blur on the text and sparkles instead of crisp pixels.
The title lettering is smooth vector-style serif type with glow, not pixel-grid lettering, which weakens the 8-bit rule. The columns have gradient or noise texture rather than clean flat pixels.

At thumbnail size, the bear shrinks to a tiny blob and the rainbow merges into a thin strip. Only 'GRADUATION' and, faintly, 'KANYE WEST' stay legible. The 2007, copies line and category label turn to mush, and the balloons are small colored specks.
The side balloons are cut off or crowded at the edges and carry little weight relative to the focal figure. The bottom 'ARTS & CULTURE' line is very low contrast, dark purple on near-black.
critic.next_change: Fix the stat line: widen the yellow box to span the full text with at least 12px of padding on each side (or shorten the text to '957,000 #1 BILLBOARD'), and make sure it does not overlap the gold columns.
critic.works: Subject and style land well. The pixel-art teddy bear in a graduation outfit with shades is a clear nod to Kanye's Graduation cover. The rainbow arc, popsicle balloons, gold columns and sparkles are vivid 8-bit elements on a dark starfield. The neon title hierarchy of yellow name, large pink GRADUATION and cyan 2007 reads well at full size. The palette is saturated and nostalgic.

fails: The flame sprites sit behind the title and the Top Fires panel. The big flame runs through 'CALIFORNIA' and 'WILDFIRES', and the glow and pixel blocks run through the right panel's lines (HARRIS, POOMACHA, SANTIAGO / MANZANITA). That hurts legibility and looks like a layering mistake.
The fire row is a horizontal strip with a large flat dead black band below it (y~620-820). It looks like unfinished space, and the composition is top-heavy and fragmented into disconnected boxes.

The Top Fires list and the 'SANTA ANA WINDS' and 'RICE / GUEJITO' lines are dark orange on near-black at a tiny size, so contrast is very low even at full size. The top-left orange pixel squiggle is an unexplained, clipped-looking shape.

The background is smooth gradients and dim scanlines rather than crisp flat pixel art, so it reads as muddy and murky instead of vibrant 8-bit. There is no landscape, hills, houses or sky to anchor the scene, so the fire has no sense of place. The grey/blue squares inside the flames look like stray artifacts.

At 120px the headline turns into a smear of yellow and orange. Everything below the title, including both info boxes and the date, is illegible, and the flames read as a thin glowing line, so there is no strong silhouette.
critic.next_change: Move the flame sprites out from behind the text panels. Put one large, bright, flat-colored pixel fire with a dark silhouetted hill/house skyline across the empty lower-middle band (y~620-820), and shrink or drop the right-hand Top Fires panel so the headline sits on clean dark ground.
critic.works: The palette is on-theme: a dark ember ground with a red-orange-yellow fire gradient and stepped pixel flame blocks, which suggests a wildfire. The headline is large, in a monospace pixel-style face, and colored from yellow to orange to red. The text is specific to this article (OCT 21, 2007, 369,000 acres, the named fires, Santa Ana winds 60+ MPH). The framed panels with corner brackets suit the 8-bit UI look.

fails: The title overlaps the car. The wheels and lower body sit directly on top of the 'TRANSFORMERS' lettering, and the car is clipped by it.
The subtitle 'PIXEL EDITION' is crammed against the bottom border and nearly touches it. It is thin, widely spaced cyan on a dark ground, so it is low contrast and not pixel-styled.
The Decepticon is a large flat gray mass on a dark navy ground. It has low contrast and little internal detail, so it reads as a blob. The Autobot is much more vivid, which unbalances the two robots.
The dashed lines from the cube to each robot are faint, anti-aliased diagonals. They are not pixel-aligned and break the 8-bit rule.
The glows behind the robots are smooth radial gradients, and the cube has a smooth ellipse halo. Both contradict the clean pixel-graphics requirement.
The AUTOBOTS and DECEPTICONS labels use small serif type that is not pixel-styled and is tiny at thumbnail size.
Neither robot is clearly Optimus Prime or Megatron. Both are generic blocky robots, and the Autobot's head and chest are muddled.

At 120px the robots and cube survive as silhouettes, but the title shrinks to a smudge that is half covered by the car. The car merges into the title block, and the subtitle and labels are unreadable.
critic.next_change: Move the yellow car up and out of the title band, or shrink it and place it clearly above the title baseline, so the wheels no longer overlap the 'TRANSFORMERS' lettering. Then swap the gray Decepticon fill for a lighter steel/purple palette with a bright outline so it separates from the background.
critic.works: The subject is clear and fits the film. The Autobot and Decepticon robots face off, the AllSpark cube sits between them, and a yellow Bumblebee-style car is in front. The style is credibly 8-bit: blocky pixel shapes, a saturated palette, a CRT-style grid floor, a starfield, a gold border with corner brackets, and a chunky title with a drop shadow. The red/blue Autobot against the gray/purple Decepticon gives a clear value and color split, and the title is legible at full size.

fails: Style: the glow halos, blurred beam and gradient fades read as modern vector or neon, not strict 8-bit pixel art. The pyramid is a smooth triangle with thin lines, not a blocky pixel grid. Several elements have anti-aliased soft edges.

Craft: the Fallen is dark maroon on a dark purple sky and has very little value separation. The grey middle robot is a muddy, unreadable blob that looks like a leftover shape. The brown rock at lower left is also unclear.

Craft: the cyan and orange laser streaks and the small orange/yellow explosion cluster are tiny and scattered, so they add noise instead of a clear focal point. The two grey ships are low-contrast and ambiguous.
Craft: the '8-BIT MODE' tag and the yellow corner brackets are small decoration that adds clutter without helping the subject.

Thumbnail: at 120px the title text turns to mush and the secondary lines are illegible. The Fallen almost vanishes. Only the pyramid and beam, the blue and red robot and the title box survive as shapes.
critic.next_change: Redraw the Fallen and the grey middle robot with hard-edged pixel blocks. Give the Fallen a lighter rim or fill (for example bright red and orange with a gold horn highlight) so it separates from the dark sky. Delete the grey blob and the glow or blur filters on the pyramid and beam, and replace them with stepped, flat-colour pixel steps.
critic.works: The subject is specific and recognisable: an Optimus-style red and blue robot, a horned dark Decepticon (the Fallen), a pyramid, and a Star Harvester beam firing into a sun. All of these come straight from the article. The title card is clean and legible at full size. The warm orange, gold and cyan palette is coherent. The robots and the pyramid have a clear silhouette against the dusk sky.

fails: Style: the devices are smooth flat vector rectangles with rounded corners, soft glows, and anti-aliased type. The 'iOS 4 & THE APP STORE' headline and the callouts use a smooth sans-serif with a blurry glow instead of a blocky pixel font, so it reads as neon flat design rather than 8-bit pixel art. Only the tiny App Store glyph is pixelated.

The App Store icon glyph is a malformed, off-center 'A' with no crossbar or legs. It is stepped and ambiguous, and it sits in the upper half of the tile, so it does not read as the real App Store logo.

The subject is drawn too generically. The two handsets look like the same slab, the tablet is mostly an empty dark lower half, and the phones carry no iOS 4 feature such as folders or multitasking, so little distinguishes iOS 4 from other iOS versions.

The composition is cluttered. There are many tiny floating app tiles, dotted connector lines that stop short of the devices, a '300,000 APPS' box that overlaps a pink tile, and a stray dark square in the lower-left corner of the title frame. The 'VERSION iOS 4' label is small and low-contrast, and the '300,000 APPS' text is repeated in the callout and the subtitle.
Thumbnail: the three devices and the title block survive as silhouettes. 'ECOSYSTEM', the date line and the callouts turn to mush, the centered App Store icon is lost, and the glow blurs the title.
critic.next_change: Redraw the whole banner on a coarse pixel grid. Use crisp-edged rects with shape-rendering=crispEdges, a chunky blocky pixel typeface for the title built from rects or a pixel font, no glows or gradients, and a rebuilt App Store glyph. Remove the floating tiles and the stray square.
critic.works: The banner depicts the actual subject. It shows an iPhone-style handset, a larger iPad-style tablet, and a central App Store icon. A 'VERSION iOS 4' label and a '300,000 APPS' callout tie it to the article's facts. The neon teal, orange and yellow on a dark ground is vibrant and retro-arcade. The title is large, high-contrast and legible at full size, and the corner-bracket frame works as a clean HUD-style border.

fails: The title and date are rendered in smooth glowing vector type, not pixel or bitmap lettering. This breaks the 'clean pixel graphics' rule, and the glow and scanline blur make it look more like synthwave than 8-bit.

The castle, flags and stripe edges are blurred by glow and scanline overlays, with no hard pixel grid. The flags and handshake are chunky blocks rather than true pixel art. The hand/arm strip reads as a beige bar with blue cuffs, not as a handshake.

The castle is a dim purple on near-black, so the focal point is weak. The missiles, arrows and treaty document are small and clustered, and the treaty page overlaps the castle gate and the horizon line.

The footer text (OBAMA + CLINTON, MEDVEDEV + LAVROV, VERIFICATION REGIME...) is tiny, thin and low-contrast. The two '1,550' boxes are nearly invisible against the dark base. Together they are clutter that adds nothing at card size.
At 120px the headline is a smudge, the date line is unreadable, and the castle, missiles and handshake collapse into a blob. Only the two flags and the framed title bar survive as shapes.

The US flag is cropped by the title frame and the Russian flag has no canton detail. The two flags differ in size and position relative to the poles, and the flagpoles are thin gray lines that are barely visible.
critic.next_change: Delete the footer text and the two 1,550 boxes, and enlarge the title to a bold blocky bitmap-style font, built from rects or a pixelated font with shape-rendering crispEdges and no glow filter. Give the castle and flags a brighter value so the central treaty/handshake motif stands out and the headline stays readable at 120px.
critic.works: Subject is specific and legible: Obama/Clinton and Medvedev/Lavrov are named, with the US and Russian flags flanking a Prague Castle silhouette. A handshake sits over a signed treaty page, a green and a red missile face each other, and matching 1,550 counters appear on both sides. The neon-cyan title and yellow date sit on a dark navy panel with strong contrast. The palette is vibrant, with scanlines and a retro HUD frame that fit the 8-bit game feel. Composition is symmetric and the story reads clearly at full size.

fails: The '[2010]' and 'SCORE: 888%' boxes overlap each other and sit on top of the Android's antennae, which is clipping and clutter at the focal point.
The Symbian phone and its label are nearly invisible against the dark background. It is the market leader in the article, but it reads as an afterthought.

The title is set in a smooth anti-aliased sans with glow, not blocky pixel lettering, and the title frame is a thin vector line. The style is closer to a CRT terminal than 8-bit game pixel art. The palette is mostly dark green rather than vibrant.
The bottom Q4 chart is tiny. Its labels (AND/iOS/BB/WP) are dark on dark, and the BB and WP labels are unreadable. The chart also leaves a lot of empty space around it.
Phone labels and sub-labels are small, with low contrast for the red BlackBerry and blue WinPhone text. The row of phones is scattered at uneven heights.
At thumbnail size the title becomes mush, and the phones, labels and chart are all indistinct. Only the green frame and a faint Android blob survive.
critic.next_change: Remove the overlapping [2010] and SCORE badges (or stack them cleanly above the Android's head with a gap), then enlarge the Android bot and the title block and switch the title to chunky blocky pixel letters, so the headline and focal sprite hold up at 120px.
critic.works: The Android bot is a clear central focal point with a glow, and the pixel phones for BlackBerry, iOS and WinPhone 7 each use their own brand colors. The green-on-black CRT palette, scanlines and bordered title frame give a coherent retro-terminal mood. The title and subtitle are crisp, well spaced and correctly wrapped. The Q4 US market bar chart and the 888% score callout both reflect the article's actual data.

fails: Style: only the car is actually pixel art. The headline, stat boxes, ticker text and candlestick chart are smooth anti-aliased vector shapes with soft glows and scanlines. They read as a modern trading dashboard, not an 8-bit game screen, which breaks the 'clean pixel graphics' rule.
The TESLA wordmark is dark red on near-black navy with a blur glow. It is the lowest-contrast item in the biggest type, so the brand name is the weakest element.
The bottom ticker lines (CEO, co-founders, DOE loan, Roadsters sold) are very dark green on black and nearly illegible even at full size. They add clutter without payoff.

Clutter: four stat boxes, a quote-style TSLA box, an EXCHANGE badge, a ticker, a chart and a car compete with each other. There is no single dominant focal point, and the left column is stacked with small text.
Stray yellow pixel crosses at the bottom of the chart area (x≈880 and x≈1500) look like orphaned artifacts. A big empty band sits under the chart, which makes the layout feel unbalanced.

The car is generic: a flat red wedge with a yellow sparkle and dark-gray wheels that blend into the background. Its edges are crisp but the shading is minimal, so it reads more as a spaceship or hovercraft than a Tesla Roadster.
Thumbnail: at 120px the headline, stat boxes and ticker are unreadable mush. Only a faint red car blob and the green candles survive as shapes. The title does not read at all.
critic.next_change: Rebuild the banner as one chunky pixel-grid composition. Drop the stat boxes, ticker, TSLA box and EXCHANGE badge. Render a large, bright, blocky-pixel red Roadster with a visible stepped silhouette on the left, and a stepped pixel-block rising bar chart with an '8-bit' pixel font 'TSLA IPO' headline in bright white or yellow on the right. Use hard-edged rects only, with no blur filters or smooth text.
critic.works: The subject is specific and correct: TESLA, IPO, June 29 2010, NASDAQ, $17 offer, $226M raised, $23.89 close and +40.5% all appear. The rising green candlestick chart with a highlighted IPO candle is a clear focal element. The pixel-block red roadster nods to the Roadster. The dark navy ground with neon green, cyan and amber gives a vibrant arcade mood.

fails: Subject is generic: the Murdoch testimony is shown only by two tiny, near-identical figures, and neither reads as Rupert Murdoch. The newspaper (News of the World) is a vague gray page, and the foam pie / gavel / lamp props are hard to identify.
The scene is cluttered and disconnected. The gray lamp-like object above the figures, the floating foam splash, the sign and the desk all sit at different scales and don't share a single focal point.
The newspaper at lower left is cropped against the Parliament building and overlaps the windows, so it looks pasted on. Its masthead and icon are illegible mush.
The '2011' badge top right is a flat black box with green text, drawn in a different, non-pixel style, and its edges are not aligned with the frame.
The 'PRESS SELECT TO TESTIFY' line is small and dim gold on dark, and the 'LEVESON INQUIRY' sign text is low-contrast gray on red. Both are weak even at full size.

At 120px the headline is unreadable, and the scene shrinks to a dark mass in which only Big Ben's green tower and the red/yellow title frame are distinguishable. The figures, sign and newspaper vanish.
The palette is mostly dark navy and murky, so it is less 'vibrant' than the style card asks for. The type is smooth, anti-aliased and glowing rather than a blocky pixel font.
critic.next_change: Cut the scene to one large focal group: scale the two figures and desk up about 2x as the hero, with a distinct white-haired Murdoch silhouette in a bright color against the lit Parliament. Delete the lamp, foam splash and gavel clutter and the pasted-on newspaper. Replace the title with a shorter, larger blocky pixel-font line such as 'MURDOCH TESTIFIES' or 'PHONE HACKING 2011'.
critic.works: The pixel-art look is convincing, with a dithered night sky, a stepped Big Ben, lit windows on the Parliament block, a CRT scanline overlay and an 8-bit 'PRESS SELECT TO TESTIFY' prompt. The two blue-suited figures at the desk, the red 'LEVESON INQUIRY' sign and the newspaper at left tie it to the article. The red-bordered title box with white and yellow caps is high-contrast and clean.

fails: The 2015→2020 timeline strip and the handshake are tiny, low-contrast, and muddled. The blue blob on the strip is unreadable, and the hand sits awkwardly on the ground line, so the Platform concept isn't communicated.
The red figure at far left looks like an unidentified torch or tower. It is ambiguous and visually disconnected from the rest of the scene.

The top subtitle is smooth anti-aliased sans text in thin teal that is low-contrast against the navy sky. It clashes with the chunky pixel style elsewhere, and the star pixels collide with the lettering.
The title is set in a smooth, glowing, blurred monospace face rather than true pixel lettering, which breaks the 8-bit rule. The soft glow and gradient banding in the sky also read as non-pixel.
Dark cloud blobs at the top right nearly vanish into the sky. The dead zones left and right of the skyline leave the composition scattered, with many small unrelated props and no single focal point.
At 120px the headline turns to illegible mush, and only the green skyline, sun, and Earth survive. The subtitle, timeline, hand, and flag all vanish.
critic.next_change: Cut the clutter (timeline strip, hand, red torch figure, dark clouds, top subtitle) and enlarge the title. Re-letter it as blocky pixel-grid glyphs about 2x taller on the dark panel, with a flat hard-edged fill and no glow, so it survives at 120px.
critic.works: Clear pixel-art language with a strong palette: blue pixel Earth, glowing yellow sun, green skyline, and a bordered CRT-style title card. The story reads: 195 nations, Durban, a 2015 to 2020 timeline, and the striped South African flag, so the subject is specific. The top-to-bottom value structure is solid, with a dark sky and a bright green horizon line.

fails: The headline collides with the artwork. 'TECHNOLOGY & BROADCASTING' sits on the top of the TV bezel. The date line and colour bar run through the TV's 'LIVE' label and the left lamp post, so 'LIVE' is clipped and the date is partly unreadable.

The style is only partly obeyed. The title and stat text are smooth anti-aliased vector type, not pixel font. The background is a soft gradient with scanlines, and the HD badge, phone and 4G text are flat rectangles. This reads as a modern flat infographic with pixel accents, not clean 8-bit.

The composition is scattered and has no clear focal point. The NBC tag, '4G' and signal bars float unanchored, and the rainbow glitch line cuts through the middle of the scene. The lower-left (rings, Big Ben, stadium) is small and disconnected, with a large empty purple void between it and the stat strip.

Some items are cramped or garbled. The 4G signal bars overlap the glitch line. The tiny captions ('219.4M US VIEWERS', 'GoPro CAM') are far too small. 'FIRST EVER ALL SPORTS IN HD' is crammed into its tile. The phone's top-bar overlaps the HD badge, and the thin gray antenna mast is unexplained.

The thumbnail fails. At 120px the title, subtitle and stat tiles are mush, and the TV, phone and landmarks shrink to specks. Only the cyan corner brackets and the overall dark purple field survive, so there is no readable silhouette.
critic.next_change: Pull the headline and date out of the TV's area. Shorten the title to a large pixel-font '2012 LONDON' in the top-left with a smaller 'TECH & BROADCAST' below. Move the TV down and scale it up as the single centered hero so it fills the middle. Delete the stray NBC, 4G, glitch-line and tiny-caption clutter, and keep only the TV, the HD badge and the rings.
critic.works: The subject is clearly this article. It shows a CRT-style TV with a pixel sprinter on a track, an HD badge, a phone with 150M TWEETS, a GoPro camera, Olympic rings, Big Ben, and stat tiles for BBC 2,500 hrs, 3.6 billion viewers, <200ms timing and all sports in HD. The neon-on-dark palette is vibrant, and the pixel sprinter, rings and Big Ben do read as 8-bit.

fails: The glow and blur effects on the title, the score numbers and the neon frames break the 'clean pixel graphics' rule. The title has a magenta ghost offset that reads as a double-printing error. The type is a smooth sans-serif, not a pixel font, and the character sprites use few pixels.
The subtitle 'AND VICE PRESIDENTIAL DEBATE' is crossed by the yellow marker tick below the title, and the tick looks like a stray shape.

The VP debate is barely represented. There is one moderator and only two candidates, with no Biden or Ryan and no sign of the four-debate structure. The Obama podium logo is an ambiguous bracket shape.
The speech-bubble boxes hold generic placeholder lines. The bubble tails are tiny squares that float disconnected from the heads.

The faces are tiny and nearly identical in structure, and Obama and Romney are only distinguishable by skin tone and suit color. There is a lot of empty dark navy in the stage, and the small captions (OBAMA, MODERATOR, ROMNEY, ELECTORAL VOTES, FINAL SCORE) are too small to read.
At 120px the title shrinks to a smudge, and the HP bars, labels, chips, caption and flags turn to noise. Only the red and blue podium masses and the 332/206 score block still read.
critic.next_change: Remove the glow, blur and magenta offset on the title and numerals and set them in a chunky blocky pixel typeface at a larger size with a hard 1-2px dark drop shadow. The headline and score would then stay crisp and legible at thumbnail scale and match the clean 8-bit style.
critic.works: The subject is clearly the 2012 debates. Blue Obama and red Romney podiums, a neutral moderator desk, the VS badge, flags, HP bars, and a 332 vs 206 electoral score all tie to the article. The arcade-fighting-game framing (HP bars, 'INSERT COIN TO DEBATE') is a clever fit for the 8-bit style. The blue/red/magenta palette is vibrant and balanced left to right, and the composition is symmetric with a clear center.

fails: The gold figure at upper right is a mushy, illegible blob. It could be a hazmat or radiation figure, but it has no clear silhouette and looks like a rendering error. It is the largest competing shape and has no clear meaning.

The palette is dark and muted: near-black green ground, desaturated grey-green buildings, and a dim scanline overlay. This contradicts 'vibrant colors'. The scene reads as a dim CRT terminal rather than a bright, nostalgic 8-bit game.
The bottom ~170px is an empty navy slab. The scene sits in the middle band, and the caption floats low-contrast on a dark strip, so the composition is top- and middle-heavy with dead space.
The caption line ('OHI REACTOR 3 ONLINE...') is tiny, dim teal on dark and widely letterspaced. It is unreadable at full size without effort and is mush at thumbnail size.

Several details look off-grid or mismatched: the stray green diagonal pixel fragment beside the right building, the tiny confetti-like figures at the calendar's sides, and a grey rail strip under the left buildings. They add noise without meaning.
The calendar is the central narrative element but is small and low-contrast (thin green border, dim cells), so it gets lost against the sun.

At 120px, the two title lines shrink to indistinct smudges. The 'FUKUSHIMA DAIICHI' line is barely legible and the amber subtitle is not. Only the red sun and the gold blob survive as shapes. The buildings and calendar disappear into the dark ground.
critic.next_change: Replace the gold blob at upper right with a clear, high-contrast pixel icon (a bright yellow-and-black radiation trefoil, or a cooling tower with a glowing core). At the same time, brighten the scene by raising the building and ground colors to saturated 8-bit hues and cutting the dark scanline overlay. The trefoil gives a readable focal point at thumbnail size, and the brighter colors fix the vibrancy failure.
critic.works: The Japanese-flag red sun, the cooling-tower and factory silhouettes with pixel steam, the July 2012 calendar with the 1st and 18th marked (matching the Ohi restarts), and the green CRT-style palette all fit the article. The pixel-stepped sun and the chunky title lettering read as 8-bit. The two-tone title (green over amber) is legible at full size.
